title: Valencia: explicit faith for Apostles Creed; implicit enough for other truths in laypeople
source_text: XXXI. Gregorius autem de Valentia tractans quaestionem hanc, An scilicet necessarium sit ad salutem credere explicite omnia quae fidei sunt, vel sufficiat aliqua credere explicite? Observat primo nos habere fidem explicitam de aliqua veritate, quum elicimus assensum immediate circa ipsam: implicitam vero, quum assensum alicujus veritatis non habemus secundum seipsam, sed habemus illum quasi implicitum in alio actu nostro, qui habet aliud immediate objectum. Ut exempli causa, quum explicite & immediate credimus Scripturam esse Dei Verbum, implicite credimus omnia quae sacra Scriptura continentur, etiamsi eorum expressam notitiam non habeamus, nec de illis unquam cogitaverimus. Postea vero mentem suam explicans de proposita quaestione, asserit hoc gratiae tempore, omnibus necessarium esse explicite credere articulos illos fidei qui continentur in Symbolo Apostolorum: alias vero fidei veritates, quae praeter articulos illos in sacris literis, vel in Ecclesiae definitionibus continentur, non necessarium esse explicite credi a vulgaribus fidelibus, quibus in Ecclesia non incumbit ex officio alios erudire, & confirmare in fide; sed satis iis esse credere implicite ejusmodi veritates. Commentariorum Theologicorum in Summam Thomae, tom. 3. disput. 1. quaest. 1. puncto 5.
pass_a_gloss: Gregory of Valencia, treating whether it is necessary for salvation to believe explicitly everything that belongs to faith, or whether it suffices to believe some things explicitly, first observes that we have explicit faith concerning some truth when we elicit assent immediately about it itself; implicit faith when we do not have assent to some truth according to itself, but have it as it were implied in another act of ours that has a different immediate object. For example, when we explicitly and immediately believe Scripture is the Word of God, we implicitly believe everything contained in sacred Scripture, even if we lack express notitia of those things and have never thought of them. Explaining his mind on the proposed question, he asserts that in this time of grace it is necessary for all to believe explicitly those articles of faith contained in the Apostles Creed; but other truths of faith beyond those articles, contained in the sacred letters or in definitions of the Church, need not be believed explicitly by ordinary faithful who are not bound by office in the Church to teach others and confirm them in the faith; for them it is enough to believe such truths implicitly (Comm. Theol. in Summam Thomae, tom. 3, disput. 1, q. 1, punct. 5).
pass_b_english: Valencia distinguishes explicit faith (immediate assent to a truth) from implicit faith (assent wrapped inside another act with a different immediate object), as when believing Scripture is God Word implies all it contains.

In the time of grace everyone must explicitly believe the Apostles Creed articles; other scriptural or defined truths may be held only implicitly by lay faithful not charged to teach and confirm others.

choices.why: Valencia salvation threshold for Creed vs other truths.
rejected: explicit faith of all revealed truths required of all
